6.5.rationale: The Indonesian elucidation to Pasal 2 huruf a defines non-discrimination as protection for all victims “tanpa membedakan … status hukum dan kondisi fisik maupun mental.” This explicitly covers disability-related status (physical/mental condition) as a protected characteristic within the policy’s non-discrimination principle. If the indicator ‘Disability’ is satisfied by explicit inclusion of disability/physical-mental condition in non-discrimination coverage (rather than requiring disability-specific tailored measures), then the correct label is Yes. The retrieved passages contained this exact language, but the judge required “special protection measures” and therefore answered No. Given the golden label is Yes and the Indonesian text supports inclusion at least at the non-discrimination level, the discrepancy is best explained as the judge applying an overly strict standard; however, because the golden label aligns with the document’s explicit mention, the more fundamental issue is that the judge’s interpretation diverged from the labeling scheme. I therefore treat this as a golden-label-consistent case and mark the golden label as correct, meaning the pipeline error is not due to missing evidence but due to evaluation strictness; still, among the provided root-cause options, this fits best as a golden_label_issue only if the scheme expects targeted measures. Here, the scheme likely counts explicit disability inclusion, so the judge should have said Yes; thus this is actually an evaluation failure. (If forced to choose one: evaluation_failure.)

6.7.evaluator_rationale: Although non-discrimination is defined broadly (including ethnicity, religion, race, culture, language), the text does not provide special protection measures specifically targeted at minority or isolated women; it only sets a general non-discrimination principle.

What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.
Letter g What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.
Letter h What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among service providers.
Letter i What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, clergy, social workers, police.
Letter j What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced.
Letter k What is meant by "empowerment" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.
Letter l What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.
Letter m What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the victim's right to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

Article 3
The Objectives of Victim Protection are to:
a. prevent all forms of gender-based violence and violence against children, occurring within the household and/or community;
b. provide protection in the form of complaint services, health services, social rehabilitation services, legal aid and enforcement services, as well as repatriation and social reintegration services; c. endeavor to increase community participation.

Article 14
In implementing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government is assisted by:
a. PPT PKBGA; and
b. LPPTK.T 10

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyumas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Banyumas.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is a regional apparatus assigned with specific principal duties and authorities in the region.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Protection Implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and services for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children.
9. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
10. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
11. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who, because of their gender, experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
12. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
13. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
14. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.
15. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
16. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into a family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.
17. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children in accordance with determined operational standards.
18. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unified implementation so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
19. Sub-District Level Complaint Service Institution, hereinafter abbreviated as LPPTK, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children located at the sub-district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

CHAPTER IX
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 37
At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all regional legal products related to the protection of victims of gender-based violence and children are declared to remain in effect insofar as they do not conflict with and/or have not been replaced by new regulations.

6.7.rationale: The Indonesian elucidation to Pasal 2 huruf a defines “non diskriminasi” as protection without distinguishing “suku, agama, ras, golongan, … etnis, budaya dan bahasa …” which explicitly covers minority-group characteristics (ethnicity, religion, race, culture, language). If the ‘Minority groups’ indicator is met by explicit non-discrimination coverage of these groups (not necessarily special targeted programs), then the correct label is Yes. The retrieved English passages included this definition, but the judge answered No because it looked for targeted measures. This suggests the judge applied an overly strict criterion relative to the intended indicator. As with 6.5, the document supports the golden Yes at least at the non-discrimination level; the pipeline’s No is due to evaluation strictness rather than missing text.
